products.heading: Service Catalog Search
products.bannerArchitectureBody: Do not sell CVM, CBS, VPC and TKE separately. IaaS should be understood as one Infrastructure Architecture Bundle. In North America, prioritise standalone products that generate revenue on their own and are easy to enter with: CDN, Media, TRTC, SMS, Token Hub.
products.bannerPrincipleBody: Do not say: buy CVM. Say: we help customers build the complete architecture they need for live streaming, short video, real-time interaction, AI, global distribution and cross-border growth.
products.cardInfrastructureBody: CVM, CBS, VPC, CLB, TKE, database and security, sold as one architecture capability set rather than SKU by SKU.
products.cardStandaloneBody: CDN, EdgeOne, TRTC, GME, VOD, MPS, CSS, SMS and Token Hub can each enter independently and prove value on their own.
products.cardStoryBody: Tell the story around the customer's business scenario -- live streaming, short video, real-time game interaction, AI, globalisation, cross-border connectivity and security -- not around product features.
products.searchPlaceholder: Search products, competitors, industries, pain points, scenarios...

products.chartKnowledgeHint: How far each product has climbed from "to learn" to "can sell".

evidence.title: BD Evidence Studio
evidence.subtitle: Separate product facts, reasonable inference and customer outcomes strictly, so no claim goes out without evidence.
evidence.guideFactBody: Stated explicitly on the website, in documentation or in a formal white paper. Safe to say directly, still qualified by product version, region and conditions.
evidence.guideInferenceBody: A reasonable deduction from the product architecture. Use may, can help, is designed to, typically.
evidence.guideOutcomeBody: Specific percentages, ROI, rollout timelines and performance improvements require a customer case, PoC, benchmark or contract data.
evidence.tableHint: Level decides whether you may state this to a customer. Keep source and last-verified current.
evidence.technicalHint: What the product actually does. Verifiable capability only.
evidence.businessHint: Potential business value, expressed with may / can help.
evidence.executiveHint: Relationship to growth, risk, cost or speed. No unverified outcomes.
evidence.safeClaimHint: For example: VOD can help reduce the number of separate services a team needs to integrate.
evidence.signalsHint: One buying or migration signal per line
evidence.proofRequiredHint: Which PoC, benchmark, case study or internal confirmation is needed
evidence.replacementsHint: Incumbent -> wedge -> trigger -> migration difficulty -> proof
evidence.learningHint: One knowledge item per line; prefix with [x] when done

story.title: Product Solution Story
story.subtitle: Organised by category, competitor, use case, customer, edge and story -- not a feature list.
story.referenceCustomersHint: Public cases or internally confirmed customers; leave blank when unknown
story.formulaBody: We help [ICP] achieve [business outcome] through [architecture / capability], proving value with [metric], and expanding into [next solution].

priority.title: Product Priority Scorecard
priority.subtitle: 1 = weak or difficult, 5 = strong or easy. Every score needs a rationale.
priority.demandHint: Is the need common and urgent across target accounts?
priority.rightToWinHint: Is there a structural advantage with credible evidence?
priority.entryHint: How easily can a first test or conversation be secured?
priority.pocHint: Can value be proven quickly within a limited scope?
priority.expansionHint: Does it pull other products with it?
priority.revenueHint: Is the potential revenue and strategic value sufficient?
priority.totalHint: The system suggests a priority from this score
priority.rationaleHint: Market signals, customer need, Tencent advantage, migration difficulty, PoC conditions, expansion path
priority.validationHint: Which scores still need confirmation from a mentor, SA, customer or public evidence?

accounts.heading: Account Pipeline
accounts.bannerWorkspaceBody: Every target account gets its own research page for company events, tech stack, hiring, funding, current cloud, triggers, buying committee, account thesis and evidence sources. Complete the first 20 accounts first.
accounts.bannerThesisBody: Why this account - why now - what pain - what wedge - who buys - what proof - what next. Do not write a company profile; form a sales hypothesis that discovery can confirm or disprove.
accounts.searchPlaceholder: Search company, industry, contact, pain point...

research.title: Account Research Workspace
research.companySnapshotHint: Business model, main products, customers, regions, size
research.recentNewsHint: Funding, launches, acquisitions, international expansion, leadership changes
research.fundingHint: Funding stage, revenue growth, cost pressure, profitability targets
research.stackHint: Cloud, Kubernetes, CDN, database, AI stack, GitHub clues
research.hiringHint: Which cloud, video, security or AI roles are open?
research.vendorsHint: AWS, Azure, GCP, Cloudflare, Agora and similar
research.triggersHint: Why might a purchase or migration happen now?
research.painsHint: Cost, latency, security, expansion, delivery speed, vendor fragmentation
research.gapsHint: What is still unknown? Where will you verify it next?
research.thesisFormulaBody: Because [trigger/change], this account may face [specific pain]. Tencent Cloud can enter through [wedge] for [buyer], prove value through [metric/POC], and expand into [next products].
research.sourcesHint: Links, documents, conversations that back the thesis
research.confidenceHint: How strongly is this thesis supported today?

sop.heading: Customer Development SOP
sop.stage0Body: Chase only accounts where Tencent has a structural advantage: China-linked, Asia latency, gaming/media/RTC, cross-border, security attack, AI bilingual or multimodal.
sop.stage1Body: Write down what the customer uses now, why it might change, which product enters first, who will care, and what success looks like.
sop.stage2Body: Priority order: internal customer records, Tencent ecosystem/investment/gaming/WeChat relationships, cloud partners, events, targeted LinkedIn outreach, cold email.
sop.stage3Body: Confirm business goals, architecture, traffic and data volume, current contract, migration window, decision makers, blockers, compliance and budget.
sop.stage4Body: Turn "we are better" into measurable metrics: latency, packet loss, concurrency, cost per TB, transcode quality, attack mitigation, RPO/RTO.
sop.stage5Body: Establish the incumbent baseline, migration cost, risk mitigation, commit, support, legal and procurement timeline, and lock a mutual action plan.

playbooks.heading: Entry Playbooks
playbooks.bannerLibraryBody: Every motion is a reusable acquisition and advance play: from opportunity, trigger and ICP through wedge, POC, success metrics, expansion and evidence.
playbooks.bannerUsageBody: Find accounts through the trigger, validate with discovery, then choose one wedge to enter a PoC. A motion is not a fixed answer; it is a set of hypotheses that customer facts must confirm.
playbooks.subtitle: Form a complete execution path from market signal to close and expansion.

weekly.answerPlaceholder: Write the answer for this week
